title: Music in Carlton and his uncle who played with famous bands
summary: He cannot recall bands in Carlton; he speaks of his uncle Johnny St. Cyr and the hardship of older musicians.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: See, I was wondering how, what the difference would be in the music you'd hear on Perdido Street in that neighborhood when you were living there? And up in Carlton? It's all the same. All the same, huh? Yeah, all the same. And what would you hear up in Carlton? Do you remember any of that?

He asked me, me and Ragtime, he was the Carlton in them days. And who would be playing at the bar? Well, I don't know. I know my uncle Johnny Sing said he was playing with some band up there, but I can't recall who it was, because I never heard him mention his name.
And how many guys in the band? Do you remember the band that band? It was four then, at that time, I remember. What was your uncle playing?

He didn't even have no drum with him. He was playing Ghetto at that time. Uh-huh. He was taking up banjo in later years. That's when he went with Louis. He plays occasionally at, you know, like all weekends out there in California.

Well, guys like that, they aren't good enough to work. They only work with Louis Armstrong, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and all the rest of them. And yet today they're not working. Isn't that funny?
They're not good enough for this town.

Being with famous men like that, they look like they should get up plenty of work, but they don't. See, most of his work is flashing now. But he do work on Friday and Saturday and Sunday nights, I believe. On weekends out in Los Angeles. I don't know what particular spot he's working at now. I know the last I heard him and Elton's playing at one place and Buddy Burns, he's playing somewhere else. It just splits up, you know. Sometimes they come together on jobs.
